day.sun: Euler(55,135,0): 55 deg elevation, shadows toward +x/-z, i.e. away from the follow, wide, sideline and diagonal cameras (+z side) and from the behind-goal camera (-x). Least dot(shadow, camera view) over the five v98 cameras and a 9x5 ball grid = 0.178 (follow camera, ball at the far-left corner), > 0 everywhere. Colour (1,.962,.89), intensity 1.5, shadow strength .86.

day.grading: contrast 4, saturation 4, postExposure 0, vignette .15/.5, bloom off. With HDR off (ProbeWeb m_SupportsHDR false) any bloom threshold above ~1.4 is identical to off; off also saves the bloom passes.

lightLookContractForStadiumLane.struct: MatchLightCondition.cs unchanged (frozen fields). Values: MatchLighting.NightLook / DayLook; ProbeBridge.LightLook is set as the first statement of ApplyMatchLighting, which BuildStadium calls before any stadium texture is built.
lightLookContractForStadiumLane.light: MatchLight.Night for legacy and night presentation, Day for day presentation. Lane C must not infer 'legacy' from it; legacy = string.IsNullOrEmpty(presentation?.schema) (or ProbeBridge.Look == MatchLook.Legacy).
lightLookContractForStadiumLane.skyTop/skyHorizon/skyGround: sRGB colours for the generated sky dome texture, same space as the existing skyTex code (night values reproduce it exactly).
lightLookContractForStadiumLane.lampEmission: multiplier on the existing lamp emission (1.6,1.5,1.3); night 1, day 0 (lamps off, panels lit by the sun as albedo).
lightLookContractForStadiumLane.windowLit: GRAIN THRESHOLD, not a fraction: a generated window cell is lit when its stable grain in [0,1] exceeds windowLit (existing code: lit>.45f). .45 = Release 130 (~55 % lit); 1 = no lit windows (grain never exceeds 1).
lightLookContractForStadiumLane.crowdLight/bannerLight: multipliers on the spectator/supporter and banner base colours (1 = Release 130). Day < 1 because the sunlit far stand faces the sun (about 2.5x the evening light on the crowd); keeps crowds below the kits.

shadows.keyLights: One shadow-casting light in every look (the scene's directional light). No additional lights.
shadows.map: Received looks: standard 2048 soft, reduced 1024 hard; one cascade; shadowDistance = MatchLighting.ShadowDistance(length,width) = (follow-camera far-corner distance + 5 m)/(1-0.12): 91.9 m on 68x44, 107.6 m on 81.6x52.8; cascadeBorder (fade) .12. Set once per load, never per frame (stable sphere fit).
shadows.fade: URP's GetMainLight(shadowCoord) used by the D6 shaders has no distance fade, so a shorter distance would make far shadows pop at the cascade sphere. Received looks apply URP's own fade (GetMainLightShadowFade) in D6Pitch, WorldKit and D6Blob, like URP Lit already does for lines/ball/posts.
shadows.bias: Received looks: depth 1 / normal 1 shadow texels (URP defaults) set on BOTH the light and the pipeline asset, so the effective bias no longer depends on whether the Sun has UniversalAdditionalLightData (URP uses the light's bias only with usePipelineSettings=false; ProbeSetup created the Sun via AddComponent, so G0 most likely ran on the pipeline's 1/1 and the light's .04/.35 was inert). MatchLightingTests reports the actual source.
shadows.figures: WorldKit's caster (only with _D6_LOOK) scales URP's per-light _ShadowBias by .3 depth / .12 normal (D6ShadowClipScaled): with the full normal bias (2.5 texels x ~7 cm soft kernel) the flat-shaded low-poly facets part and the limbs vanish from the map, and the full depth bias lifts the shadow off the boots. Kit self-shadow acne is handled on the receiver: the kit looks its shadow up 12 cm along its normal and takes 30 % of it (standard); reduced skips the lookup (weight 0, cheaper, no hard-shadow banding).
shadows.ball: The 35 cm ball would vanish under the full normal bias, so received looks give it a shadow-only twin (MeshRenderer 'Ball shadow caster', 0.88 scale, child of the ball, WorldKit material from matchKitShader) that casts with the figures' bias share; the visible ball no longer casts. 0.88 keeps the ball's own lit side out of its twin's shadow. Null-safe: without matchKitShader the ball keeps casting itself.
shadows.casters: Received looks: only figures, ball (twin), goal posts, crossbar, net supports and rear crossbar cast; pitch markings, net mesh, turf/apron boxes, blobs and all D6Env stadium parts are Off. Legacy: Release 130 casters unchanged. The hidden ground skin (FootballGround.IsGroundSkin) is never touched.
shadows.contactBlobs: D6Blob _Model 1 (received looks) splits the turf light like D6Pitch into the shadowable key (light strength k, raw shadow), its unshadowed rest and the sky: the core blocks _Contact of the key (what the map cannot resolve at the boots), the disc blocks _Occlusion of rest+sky. In a cast shadow only the occlusion term remains, so nothing darkens twice. Players: strength 1, contact .7/.78, occlusion .34/.30, core .55/.50 (night/day). Ball: contact .95, occlusion .50/.45, core .75/.70; its _Strength stays driven per frame by WorldViewPresentation.BallShadowStyle (native-height logic untouched). Disc sizes unchanged (players 1.05, ball from BallShadowStyle).
shadows.kitsHighlight: Received looks apply a soft shoulder above knee .82 (night) / .62 (day) to the lit kit colour: front-lit white/bright kits in the sun keep distinct facet tones instead of clipping to one white in the LDR picture (slope 1 at the knee; darker kits, skin and the night camera-facing sides are below the knee and unchanged).

quality.reduced: MSAA off (camera and pipeline), bloom off, 1024 hard shadows, kit shadow lookup skipped. Standard: pipeline MSAA (4 in ProbeWeb), bloom only at night.
quality.restore: RestoreProbeLighting restores ambient, light (rotation, colour, intensity, shadows, strength, depth AND normal bias), camera (background, MSAA, far, renderPostProcessing and renderShadows to their captured values instead of the old forced false), pipeline (resolution, distance, MSAA, cascade count, cascade border, depth and normal bias), _D6LowPoly 0 and the _D6_LOOK keyword off.

contractDeviationsForRootReview: Shadow distance: the contract expected 55-75 m; measured from the actual follow-camera rig the far pitch corner is 75.9 m (68x44) / 89.7 m (81.6x52.8), so full-strength coverage needs 91.9/107.6 m incl. margin and fade. Still below G0's 110 m standard (finer texels). Reduced follows the same rule as the contract demands, which makes reduced texels ~30 % coarser than G0's 70 m reduced; if the Pixel shows a regression, a reduced-only constant is a one-line change in ApplyMatchLighting.
One cascade instead of up to two: URP does not blend cascades, the seam would cross the pitch and move with the camera, and two cascades at 2048 halve each tile.
Day bloom off instead of a raised threshold (identical picture in LDR, cheaper).
Kits receive 30 % of the shadow map (standard) with a 12 cm receiver offset instead of full self-shadowing; players in another player's shadow darken less than the turf.
Ball casts through a shadow-only twin; the visible ball's own renderer is Off in received looks.
Pitch markings and the net stop casting in received looks (sub-texel; only cost shadow passes).
Night keeps the Release 130 key direction, so night shadows still fall toward the broadcast camera, as the contract's night base requires.
